quotes.text: The architecture required to prepare for quantum computing is fundamentally incompatible with how you're building AI systems today. This is not a technical problem. It's a governance problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's central thesis that quantum readiness is a governance redesign, not a tech upgrade.

quotes.text: Co-pilot isn't the endpoint. It's the entry point to a much larger orchestration problem that most organizations haven't mapped yet.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Copilot as the start of a broader orchestration and governance challenge.

quotes.text: The problem isn't that your encryption is weak today. The problem is that it will be weak tomorrow and you are storing data today that still has value in the future.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the harvest-now-decrypt-later risk in one clear sentence.

quotes.text: If you have data labeled must remain confidential for 20 years, that label needs to automatically trigger a requirement for post-quantum encryption.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, actionable link between data classification and quantum-safe encryption.

quotes.text: Governance is not a feature you add at the end. It is not a module you just plug in. It is the foundational logic that determines if a system is actually trustworthy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why governance must be designed in before quantum workloads arrive.

takeaways: Classical M365 governance is binary, Copilot and AI agents are probabilistic, and quantum adds superposition, so governance must be redesigned to span all three.
Harvest-now-decrypt-later makes long-lived M365 data vulnerable today, so organizations need a cryptography inventory, confidentiality horizons and a crypto agility roadmap.
Hybrid quantum-classical workloads need decision gates, quantum-safe identity and key management, end-to-end audit trails and portability before any pilot touches real data.
hook: Your AI governance is built on binary rules, Copilot reasons in probabilities, and quantum computing will add a third logic entirely. This episode shows M365 governance and Azure architecture leaders why quantum-safe cryptography, crypto agility and hybrid governance gates have to be designed now, before quantum-classical workloads go live.
